# Proper deepest inputs and a disjoint atomic parity budget

This is a structural theorem for the established positive concave-energy
buffer. It does not assume a minimizing body, cap differentiability, a
regular circuit, or singleton deepest faces. It does not pay the mixed
atomic/proper objective by itself.

The dependencies are joint projective-energy concavity and its full
marked-homothety equality classification, the positive concave multiplier
construction, finite tilt compression, and the whole-fiber/base-gap lemma.
The new combination is that a strict-base-gap deepest base cannot be made
from any atomic deepest input. This improves the number of atomic covering
caps from k(I) to k(I)-k(J).

## 1. Actual setting and definitions

Let P be a finite lattice-complete base in its inherited affine lattice,
with positive compatible d-dimensional convex fibers K_z. Let C be their
canonical convex hull, M their total mixed volume, and ell a positive
continuous concave function on conv(P). Positive affine ell is included.
Fix epsilon>0 and a positive definite norm
Gamma on continuous normals. The covariance norm is an allowed choice.
At real points of C put

    f(z,X)=[ell(z) E_(C_z)(X)/M]^(1/(d+1)).             (1)

This is jointly continuous, concave, positive at fiber-interior points,
and zero on fiber boundaries. The multiplier may have the arithmetic or
geometric normalization: neither is used in this fixed-family argument.

The raw buffered depth at w=(p,y) is the infimum of

    mu{a.(z-p)+u.(X-y)>=-epsilon f(w) Gamma(u)}          (2)

over nonzero continuous u and arbitrary base a, also minimized with the
weighted closed pure-base depth b_base(p). Let Q be the global mixed
maximum, and assume 0<Q<M. Let

    I={p in P: some mark (p,y) has buffered depth Q},
    J={p in I: b_base(p)>Q},       A=I\J.               (3)

Every p in I has b_base(p)>=Q. Thus A is exactly the pure-base-bound
deepest set, with b_base(p)=Q. We call its bases atomic only in this sense;
this does not make the positive continuous fibers point masses.

All deepest marks are interior to their fibers. At a boundary mark f=0,
an actual global support plane with a nonzero continuous normal gives a
zero-mixed-volume cap. Such a plane exists by the finite canonical support
LP, even at a boundary base. Every fiber intersection of that plane has
zero d-volume, so the asserted zero cap is valid for d=1 as well.

The real buffered superlevel set at Q is convex. In particular any
anchored convex combination of deepest marks with integer base is again
deepest. Therefore I=P intersect conv(I). Write k(S) for the number of
occupied parity classes of S in the inherited lattice, with k(empty)=0.

## 2. Two status facts with no regularity assumption

At a deepest mark over an atomic p, EVERY own buffered trace is full.
Here is a direct proof. If one continuous direction omitted a positive
part of K_p, take an attained mass-Q pure-base cap at p and add a large
finite multiple of its base normal to that continuous direction. All
strictly positive-base fibers are full, all negative-base fibers are
empty, and zero-drift fibers contribute at most their full masses. The
own fiber contributes strictly less. Finiteness of P and boundedness of
the fibers then give a buffered cap of mass strictly below Q, impossible.
Equivalently, this is the equality branch of the exact base-gap criterion.

At a deepest mark over r in J, an active nonvertical cap is attained,
and EVERY such active cap has a proper own trace. Finite status-pattern
tilt compression supplies compact representatives; continuity of cap mass
then gives attainment. An own-full cap has mass at least b_base(r) by the
whole-fiber capture lemma, hence cannot have mass Q. The own trace is
not empty because the mark is interior and its positive buffer captures
a neighborhood. Thus it is proper. Other fibers can have supporting
facets; no differentiability there is needed.

## 3. Heredity of the strict-base-gap deepest set

**Theorem.** Suppose r in J has an anchored representation

    r=sum_(j=1)^m lambda_j p_j,
    p_j in I, lambda_j>0, sum lambda_j=1.               (4)

Then every input p_j belongs to J.

Choose ARBITRARY deepest marks w_j=(p_j,y_j). Their formed mark
w_r=sum lambda_j w_j belongs to C and to the convex Q-superlevel set;
its integer base is r, so its depth is exactly Q. Choose an attained
active cap at w_r, as in Section 2, and normalize Gamma(u)=1. Write

    Nw=a.z+u.X,
    c=Nw_r-epsilon f_r,         H={Nw>=c},
    mu(H)=Q.                                             (5)

For this FIXED N define the right upper quantile

    c_Q(N)=sup{t:mu{Nw>=t}>=Q}.

Its tail is continuous: u is nonzero and every fiber is positive, so
each projected law is absolutely continuous. The proper own trace at
w_r makes this tail strictly decreasing in a neighborhood of c. Thus

    c_Q(N)=c.                                            (6)

This is the only inverse-quantile fact needed. It remains valid at all
supporting incidences in other fibers and does not require a derivative.

Every input deepest mark satisfies its constraint for this same quantile:

    Nw_j-epsilon f_j<=c.                                 (7)

Averaging (7), using (5), gives sum lambda_j f_j>=f_r.
Concavity of f gives the reverse inequality. Hence

    f_r=sum lambda_j f_j,
    Nw_j-epsilon f_j=c for EVERY j.                      (8)

In particular the SAME ambient cap H is active at every input mark.

Put F_j=E_(K_pj)(y_j)^(1/d), and define F_r analogously. Equality in
the concavity chain

    f=M^(-1/(d+1)) F^(d/(d+1)) ell^(1/(d+1))

forces equality in the joint concavity of F, in concavity of ell along
this relation, and in the weighted geometric mean. Indeed the geometric
mean is strictly increasing in each positive argument, so equality also
requires ell(r)=sum lambda_j ell(p_j). Equality in the geometric mean
forces F_j/ell(p_j) to be constant. Full energy equality,
including monotonicity under the actual target inclusion, then yields
one centered convex body K_* with

    K_pj=y_j+ell(p_j) K_*,
    K_r=y_r+ell(r) K_*,
    f_j/ell(p_j)=f_r/ell(r)=c_*>0.                       (9)

For completeness the multilateral equality is obtained by grouping any
one positive input against the remaining convex combination and applying
the two-input equality theorem repeatedly. Strict monotonicity of energy
under proper inclusion rules out a larger target fiber. No smoothness or
strict convexity of K_* is assumed.

By (8), the own trace of H in the j-th fiber, after the actual change
X=y_j+ell(p_j)Y, is

    {Y in K_*:u.Y>=-epsilon c_*}.                        (10)

The same expression holds in the r-fiber. Thus its full/proper/empty
status is IDENTICAL in every input and target fiber, including boundary
contacts. It is proper at r. An atomic input would have every own trace
full by Section 2, a contradiction. This proves the theorem.

Notice the essential hypothesis epsilon>0. It is what turns equality of
the buffered constraints into equality of f. An ordinary unbuffered
claim is not being inferred by setting epsilon=0.

## 4. J is a closed minor

The real base-depth region {z:b_base(z)>Q} is convex. One way to see this
without conventions about open quantiles is that the measure is finite
atomic, so its possible halfspace masses form a finite set. Accordingly
the condition >Q equals >=Q+eta for some fixed eta>0 on its nonempty
domain, and every weighted-depth superlevel is convex.

If r in P intersect conv(J), combine deepest marks at bases in J. The
formed mark is deepest, so r in I, while convexity of the strict base-gap
region gives b_base(r)>Q. Thus

    J=P intersect conv(J).                              (11)

This is relative lattice completeness in the same inherited lattice.
It does not assert that conv(J) is a face of conv(I).

The atomic set A is also a closed minor: any r in P intersect conv(A)
is in I, and the heredity theorem forbids r in J. Thus A=P intersect
conv(A). This does not make all parities occupied by A disjoint from J;
the disjointness proved below concerns the selected atomic witnesses.

## 5. Atomic compression with parities disjoint from J

If A is empty take m=0. Otherwise for every p in A choose a closed
pure-base halfspace of mass Q containing p. None contains any point of
J: a halfspace containing j in J has mass at least b_base(j)>Q.

Write this finite initial family as H_i={a_i(z)>=b_i}. Choose
U_i>max(b_i,max_P a_i), and maximize sum c_i in the compact threshold
box b_i<=c_i<=U_i subject to covering A. This constraint is closed,
being a finite intersection of finite unions of closed conditions.
At a maximizer, every nonsaturated row has an exclusive boundary witness
p_i in A:

    a_i(p_i)=c_i,
    a_j(p_i)<c_j for j!=i.                               (12)

Indeed otherwise finiteness permits increasing that threshold slightly
without uncovering A. Saturated rows capture no P and are discarded.
Let the remaining m caps be G_i={a_i>=c_i}. They still exclude J and
cover A. Each is contained in its original mass-Q cap and contains p_i,
so its actual weighted base mass is exactly Q:

    sum_(z in P intersect G_i) V_z=Q.                    (13)

Two witnesses cannot have the same parity. Their integer midpoint r is
in I by convexity of the deepest region. By (12), it lies STRICTLY
outside every G_i. The cover of A forces r in J. But Section 3 forbids
an r in J formed from the two atomic witnesses, a contradiction.

No witness can share a parity with a point t in J either. Their integer
midpoint r lies in I. Every G_i excludes t strictly, and (12) shows that
the midpoint lies strictly outside all G_i. Again r in J would have an
atomic positive input, contradicting Section 3. Consequently

    m+k(J)<=k(I).                                       (14)

All cap inequalities are closed; their excluded J points have strict
inequalities, so no boundary tie is lost in either midpoint argument.
This proves an exact mixed-stratum strengthening of the purely atomic
compression theorem.

There is an immediate actual-volume consequence, pointed out independently
by Slab. Suppose the original family has strict quotas V_T<k(T)M/k(P)
for every nonempty proper closed minor T, and both A,J are nonempty.
The cover gives V_A<=mQ, while J is a proper closed minor. Hence

    V_(P\I)>M[1-k(J)/k(P)-m Q/M].                       (14a)

In particular I=P and Q/M<1/k(P) cannot coexist with a nonempty atomic
stratum: if J is nonempty, (14a) and (14) contradict V_(P\I)=0; if J is
empty, the atomic cover directly gives M<=mQ with m<=k(P). This is a
mass-exhaustion consequence only. It does not prove I=P at a bad minimum.

## 6. The mixed stratum itself can occur: an exact sharp count

Take d=1, P={0,1}, K_0=[-1/2,1/2], K_1=[-3/4,3/4]. The canonical hull
is a genuine compatible interval frustum, with M=5/2 and within-fiber
covariance Sigma=7/48. Let ell(z)=6-5z and epsilon^2=5/7. At the two
centers the actual physical shifts are respectively

    delta_0=1/2,        delta_1=1/4.                     (15)

At an endpoint base arbitrarily steep finite base tilts exclude the other
fiber, so its depth is exactly its own buffered interval depth. For an
interval of length L and coordinate y from its center, that depth is

    min{L,L/2-|y|+delta(0) sqrt(1-4y^2/L^2)}.            (16)

This is maximized at y=0; in this example both maxima equal Q=1, and
both maximizing marks are unique. Base depths are 1 and 3/2. Therefore

    I={0,1},       A={0},       J={1},
    m=1,           k(J)=1,      k(I)=2.                 (17)

The atomic cap {z<=0} has mass Q and excludes J, saturating (14). If
geometric normalization is desired, multiply ell by 6^(-2/5) and epsilon
by 6^(1/5); the physical buffer and every conclusion are unchanged.
Its depth Q/M=2/5 is safely above the mixed target 1/4. This is not a
counterexample or a bad-minimum claim; it shows that mixed atomic/proper
classification cannot simply be replaced by all-proper classification.

## 7. Audit of the root atomic erosion and remaining payment

The root source
`candidate f324bc23ceb65e89`
passes an independent full read. In particular, convex scalar erosion
rates preserve every incoming anchored inclusion, inner parallel volume
loss is the actual surface area times that rate, threshold compression
retains exact mass Q, and off-I gaps persist under its fixed-base positive
path. No independent shrinkage of a closed minor is used.

Applied just to the m caps in Section 5, its normalized hinge construction
still has total first loss m, and each atomic cap loses at least one.
These same convex rates may, however, change the proper groups in J.
Equation (14) alone does not control their signed cap/energy/covariance
response or the multiplier penalty. A simultaneous sharp numerical
payment remains a separate obligation.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_mixed_atomic_proper_parity_defect_transport.py`
passes 18,400 exact checks, including the actual interval calculation and
2,916 finite one-dimensional compression instances satisfying the proved
midpoint hypotheses. Those finite checks do not replace the all-dimensional
quantile, energy-equality, or parity arguments.
